To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a learning-based pipeline that is capable of automatically generating, in an efficient and scalable manner, an arbitrary number of photorealistic indoor scenes with associated ground truth data, and that we demonstrate the value of such a dataset by improving performance in various computer vision tasks and by providing benchmarks for trained models.

(1) we have developed a learning-based system for generating massive quantities of synthetic scenes and photorealistic 3D renderings thereof with ground truth data, which can be customized and controlled to enable the study of scene understanding algorithms; and (2) we have demonstrated that such data can be used to improve performance in certain machine learning-based scene understanding tasks and to provide benchmarks for and diagnostics on trained models by modifying attributes and scene properties.

we present a novel learning-based approach for the automatic generation and rendering of synthetic 3-D scenes, and we demonstrate the value of the generated scenes by improving performance in several machine-learning-based scene-understanding tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, construction, and evaluation of a pipeline for the systematic generation and rendering of 3D indoor scenes and 2D images of such scenes with associated ground truth data, for the purpose of training, benchmark testing, and diagnosing machine-learning algorithms in the fields of computer vision and robotics.

the development of an efficient pipeline for the automatic generation of massive quantities, and arbitrary numbers, of 3D synthetic scenes with associated ground truth data and photorealistic 3D renderings, which can be used to train, benchmark and diagnose learning-based computer vision, graphics, and robotics algorithms.

the design and implementation of a pipeline that is capable of generating a massive variety of indoor scenes and their corresponding images, with per-pixel ground-truth data, in an automated fashion, and that is configurable in terms of its output.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we provide a pipeline to generate a massive amount of synthetic data for training and testing of computer vision and robotics systems.

our approach provides a powerful and flexible tool for the generation of massive amounts of 3D scenes with ground truth data for training machine learning algorithms, as well as for the benchmarking and diagnostics thereof.

the proposed pipeline is a novel, learning-based, systematic, flexible, and scalable solution to the synthesis of massive quantities of photorealistic synthetic 3D indoor scenes, and their 2D images, with per-pixel ground-truth information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new tool for the computer vision and robotics communities that can be used to train, benchmark, and diagnose algorithms, and that can be used for the generation of synthetic 3d data.

we have developed an automatic, configurable, and controllable pipeline to generate massive quantities of synthetic indoor scenes, with ground truth information, that can be rendered into photorealistic images, which are then used to train, benchmark, and diagnose learning-based computer vision algorithms.
it enables the creation of a large, configurable dataset of synthetic 3d scenes and 2d images thereof, with per-pixel ground-truth information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we provide an efficient way to generate large quantities of synthetic scenes with ground truth information, thus enabling the development of machine learning-based methods for 3D scene understanding and rendering, and the evaluation of these methods.
the proposed approach enables the creation of a virtually infinite set of synthetic 2D and 3D data, which can be generated and rendered in an automated manner and with high diversity and realism.

the proposed learning-based scene synthesis pipeline can serve as a versatile and configurable tool to support the training and testing of a broad range of machine-learning-based algorithms in the computer vision, computer graphics, and robotics communities.
